clue.text: Pigeon in port briefly with stick from Brighton?

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Brighton rock is the hard sugar stick sold at the seaside
the Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A pigeon in a harbour town, perched for a moment beside a stick of seaside candy.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton rock is a stick of hard candy sold at British seaside resorts; the question mark flags that example. The clipped port then follows the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock dove is the wild ancestor of the domestic and town pigeon, so it is a species of pigeon.

clue.text: Documents contents of grey trousers

indicators.note: the contents of something are what lies inside it, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the inner pair of letters of grey
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: Paperwork describing what is stuffed in the pockets of some grey trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb or noun, records are written accounts kept as evidence, the same as documents.

clue.text: Supports children playing pianos (including Mike)

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so the letter for Mike goes in among the others
playing suggests the letters are messed about with and set in a new order

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for children
taken as written
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A parent backs the kids as they bash away at several pianos, a boy called Mike among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause or person is to argue for and back it, so champions is a verb synonym of supports.

clue.text: Party extremely permissive, duke's high?

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of the following word

blocks.note: a do is a party
the first and last letters of permissive
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: At a very relaxed party, an aristocrat is clearly under the influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone high is under the influence of drugs, which is what doped means; the question mark admits the loose fit.

clue.text: Form most of stanza number one travelling north

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter is used
in a down clue, going north means reading upward, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: a stanza is a verse of a poem
NO is the abbreviation for number
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A poem's leading verse is on the move up the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a particular form or variant of something, such as a song or a text.

clue.text: Musical composition has right person on pitch

blocks.note: a score is the written music of a composition
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A piece of music that's got a player on a sports field, or on the right note.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch suggests musical pitch, fitting the composition, but it is a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer is a player who gets a goal on a football or hockey pitch.

clue.text: Feline energy excited corgi, that's clear

indicators.note: an excited dog jumps all over the place, so the word's letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a feline is a cat
E is the symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lively cat has whipped up a corgi, plain as day.
explanation.definitionFit: A categoric statement is explicit and unconditional, leaving no doubt, which makes it clear.

clue.text: Half of standard radio confirmation

blocks.note: first meaning: the second word of the Jolly ..., the pirate flag or standard
second meaning: the word radio operators use to say a message was received

explanation.walkthrough: Half of standard looks like an instruction to take letters of the word standard, but it means half of the name of a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate flag is the Jolly Roger, and in radio procedure the same word signals message received and understood.

clue.text: Payment from King with allegiance lacking at first

indicators.note: lacking at first means missing the opening, so the word drops its initial letter

blocks.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
loyalty is allegiance

explanation.surface: A monarch receives a payment from subjects who had not been loyal to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty is a fee paid to an author or rights-holder for each copy sold or use made.

clue.text: They applaud one hundred fast movers on track?

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
runners fast enough to overtake slower ones by a full circuit

explanation.surface: An audience applauds a hundred sprinters racing round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints at the phrase like the clappers, British slang for very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Clappers are people who clap, which is to say they applaud a performance.

clue.text: Long time in enclosure being theatrical

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: an age is a long time
a sty is a pig's enclosure

explanation.surface: Being kept penned up for ages makes someone act melodramatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey behaviour is exaggerated and artificial, as if acted on a stage, so it is theatrical.

clue.text: 8's address maybe shared by Emma and Amanda

indicators.note: shared by means each of the two names contributes a part, the meeting point of the pair

blocks.note: the closing pair of letters of Emma
the opening pair of letters of Amanda

explanation.surface: Two women share a way of being spoken to.
explanation.walkthrough: Where Emma ends and Amanda begins, the joined letters read as a word; 8 is the answer to 8 down, ROYALTY, and a queen is addressed as ma'am.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma'am is the respectful form of address for the Queen and female royals, hence how royalty might be addressed.

clue.text: Quick words to music biddy regularly missed

indicators.note: regularly missed means every other letter is skipped, so the alternating survivors remain

blocks.note: rap is rhythmic speech performed over a beat
the second and fourth letters of biddy

explanation.surface: An old woman keeps missing the quick-fire lyrics of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: A biddy is a slang word for an old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and quick are adjective synonyms for something done at speed.

clue.text: Gold lining grand urinal bewildered maiden

indicators.note: something bewildered is confused, so these letters are jumbled
a lining sits inside something, so this piece goes within the others

blocks.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A young woman is baffled by a lavish gold-plated urinal.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden looks like a noun for the bewildered girl, but it is the adjective, as in a maiden voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden speech or voyage is the first one, and inaugural likewise means first, marking a beginning.

clue.text: Spectacular performer's week in quiet country

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one letter sits within the rest

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
W is the abbreviation for week
the Gulf state

explanation.surface: A star entertainer spends a week in a calm foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: A showman is a flamboyant entertainer who puts on a spectacle.

clue.text: Grandee in AGM if breaking up company

indicators.note: breaking up suggests the letters are split apart and reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A bigwig at the annual general meeting worries whether the firm is being split.
explanation.walkthrough: The word in looks like a link, but its letters are part of the mix. An AGM is an annual general meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a Venetian nobleman or any person of high rank, the same as a grandee.

clue.text: Metal spun in Shanghai and Baghdad

definitions.note: cryptic: a singer whose records are played around the world

blocks.note: first meaning: the liquid element quicksilver
second meaning: the Queen singer Freddie, whose records are played the world over

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is the band Queen; this clue's second half is cryptic, with spun meaning records played rather than anything rotating. The exact allusion behind the two cities is not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the metallic element that is liquid at room temperature, and the surname of Queen's lead singer.

clue.text: The German runner in UK crowned by one in French clothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, being crowned by something means it sits on top, so that word comes first

blocks.note: un is French for one
der is a German word for the
the Wear is a river in north-east England; a river is a runner

explanation.surface: A German athlete racing in Britain gets a French winner's crown on his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is the crossword convention for a river; the Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is the clothing worn next to the skin beneath outer garments.

clue.text: Banners Poles badly singe beforehand

indicators.note: badly done means put together wrongly, so the letters are rearranged
beforehand means coming earlier, so this mixed word is placed in front

blocks.note: taken as written
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Flags carried by Polish people were scorched carelessly ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like a nationality, or flagpoles to go with the banners, but it means the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show its nationality, so a kind of banner.

clue.text: Central section in finale came on once more

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: the core is the central part
a finale is the end

explanation.surface: The middle part of a show's grand finale returned to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An encored act is called back by the audience, so it comes on stage again after finishing.

clue.text: Two seconds hold acceptable for wrestling

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the pair wraps around a letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second and a mo is a short moment, a second
U stands for upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A wrestling hold lasting only two seconds is still allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold looks like a wrestling grip, but it tells two words for second to wrap around the U. U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling between heavyweights in a ring.

clue.text: Solo work about rascal in classical rural setting

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: An opera solo about a scoundrel, set in an idyllic countryside of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of ancient Greece, became the poets' ideal of unspoilt pastoral life.

clue.text: Calm animal, good in a hot country

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so a letter goes within the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey
the United Arab Emirates, a hot desert country
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A donkey that is well-behaved soothes nerves in a sweltering land.
explanation.walkthrough: A hot country looks like A plus a hot country, but the whole phrase gives the emirates.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or ease a feeling, so it means to calm as a verb.

clue.text: Lack of muscle on view when cold descends

indicators.note: in a down clue, descending means a letter moves lower down the column, changing the order

blocks.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A shortage of muscle is on show as a chill sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold is C, and that letter, already inside the word for view, moves two places down the column, from second to fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of something is a lack of it, so the noun absence means lack.

clue.text: Star qualities help primarily in securing many album sales

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: a char is a cleaner, a daily help
the initial letters of those five words

explanation.surface: Charm in a pop star is what mainly drives huge record sales.
explanation.walkthrough: Help looks like the first word to take an initial from, but it is a whole word: a char is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the magnetic personal appeal associated with stars, so plural charismas are star qualities.

clue.text: An age to put up place for a concert

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: taken as written
an era is an age

explanation.surface: It takes an age to erect a concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a large enclosed venue where big rock concerts are staged.

clue.text: Pieces band arranged back-to-front

indicators.note: back-to-front means the last comes first, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a strap is a band of leather or cloth

explanation.surface: A musical group sets its numbers in reverse order.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians, fitting the theme, but it is a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts are pieces or components of a whole.

clue.text: Excite highest level in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound not its spelling

blocks.note: the peak is the highest level

explanation.surface: A concert's top moment stirs the audience in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique interest or curiosity is to arouse or stimulate it, so excite is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Make another change to grass by centre of site

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
the two middle letters of site

explanation.surface: Landscaping alters the grass beside the middle of a building site again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit is to edit again, making further changes to a text or film.

clue.text: Festival star's powerful piece on PM

indicators.note: in an across clue one word on another follows it, so the piece is written after

blocks.note: Theresa May was a British prime minister
the queen is the strongest chess piece

explanation.surface: A festival's headliner gives a forceful article about the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like afternoon, but it is a prime minister, here Theresa May. Brian May of Queen fits the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The May queen is the girl crowned to preside over traditional May Day celebrations, the star of that festival.

clue.text: Clergyman made a confession to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the letters are a part of the phrase

blocks.note: spanning the end of made, a and the start of confession

explanation.surface: A priest partly owned up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: John Deacon was Queen's bassist, another of the puzzle's theme words.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest, so a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Practise on vehicle used for final journey

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
a hearse carries a coffin to the funeral

explanation.surface: Someone rehearses riding in a funeral car before their last trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance before giving it.
